build: cancel unfinished CI runs when a PR is closed

Once a PR is merged (or closed) its CI result no longer matters, but
a run that is still in progress keeps occupying runners, often for the
better part of an hour due to the itests.

Add a workflow triggered on pull_request_target closed that cancels
every unfinished run of the main CI workflow triggered by the PR's head
commit. pull_request_target is used so the token has actions: write
even for PRs opened from forks. No PR code is checked out or executed.

A PR that is closed and quickly reopened gets a fresh run for the same
head commit. To never cancel it, the handler bails out if the PR is
open again by the time it runs and only considers runs that were
created before the close event.

Only main.yml runs are targeted on purpose: the backport workflow is
triggered by the very same closed event and shares the head commit, so
a broader match would cancel it.

commit.message:
build: skip CI for docs-only changes and run a fast subset on drafts

Every push to a PR currently runs the full CI matrix regardless of what
changed or whether the PR is still being iterated on. Introduce two
measures to cut down on wasted runners while keeping all jobs in
parallel, so a single run still reports as many failures as possible:

1. A ci-gate job runs first and detects documentation-only PRs, i.e.
   PRs that only touch files under docs/ or markdown files. Renamed
   files are checked under both their old and new name so that moving
   a source file into docs/ doesn't count as a documentation change.
   The cheap commit and release notes checks always run. The way the
   other jobs are skipped depends on whether they have a matrix:

   - Non-matrix jobs (static checks, lint) and non-required jobs are
     skipped at the job level. A skipped job still reports its status,
     so the required checks in branch protection are satisfied.
   - Matrix jobs with required legs (unit tests, cross compilation,
     pinned dependencies, basic itests) are kept instantiated and skip
     their steps instead, in the same way the no-itest label already
     works. A job-level condition is evaluated before the matrix is
     expanded, so a skipped matrix job would never report the per-leg
     check names that branch protection requires and the PR would
     stay blocked.

   All job-level conditions use !cancelled() so that a failure of the
   gate job itself results in the full CI running rather than
   everything being skipped.

2. Draft PRs only run a fast subset: static checks, lint, the pinned
   dependency check, the non-race unit test legs and the basic itests
   (18-22 min per leg). The large itests (up to 86 min per leg),
   Windows and macOS itests, cross compilation, the race unit legs
   (47-56 min) and the backwards compatibility test are skipped until
   the PR is marked ready for review. ready_for_review and
   converted_to_draft are added to the pull_request trigger types so
   that changing the draft state triggers a run with the right subset;
   the concurrency group cancels the previous one.

Push and merge_group runs carry no PR and always run everything.

commit.message:
build: read live PR labels in check-label action

The check-label composite action evaluated
github.event.pull_request.labels, which is a snapshot captured when the
pull_request event fired. A label such as no-changelog or no-itest added
after the run kicked off was therefore never seen, not even when
re-running the failed job, because a re-run reuses the original event
payload. The only workaround was pushing a new commit.

Query the current label set through the API instead and only fall back
to the event payload when there is no PR number (push and merge_group
runs) or the API call fails. Re-running a failed job now picks up labels
added after the run started.

The workflow declares explicit permissions, so grant pull-requests: read
for the API call.

commit.message:
contractcourt: resolve known-preimage commitment differences

Extend commitment-difference classification to distinguish outgoing
HTLCs whose preimages are available. A forwarded HTLC learns its
preimage from the downstream peer, which the link records in the
witness beacon before accepting the commitment that removes the HTLC,
so classification and settlement consult that source alone. This
matches the source the incoming contest resolver uses for forwarded
HTLCs on chain.

Publish their terminal result through the existing resolution-message
path, keeping commitment-difference handling consistent with other
resolved HTLC states.

The sites that classify incoming HTLCs keep the registry fallback, so an
incoming HTLC paying one of our invoices still takes us to chain and
sets the sweep deadline.

commit.message:
channeldb: preserve responses during channel cleanup

Integrate the circuit-keyed forwarding response store with both channel
cleanup strategies.

Select eligible settle and fail messages before applying the forwarding
package lifecycle transition. The synchronous path updates both stores
in one transaction, while the tombstone path applies the same response
persistence rule with its existing package behavior.

This makes response state consistent across the supported database
cleanup strategies.

commit.message:
htlcswitch: retain circuits with pending responses

Extend the circuit cleanup retention predicate to include persisted
forwarding responses alongside contract-court resolution messages.

A clean store miss permits normal cleanup. Any other lookup error
preserves the current circuit state until the response state can be
determined.

Validate the new callbacks when constructing the switch because startup
uses them unconditionally.

commit.message:
htlcswitch: restore persisted forwarding responses

Load persisted forwarding responses during switch startup and send them
through the existing packet path.

Process these records before contract-court resolutions so the original
wire message takes precedence when both sources refer to one circuit.
The replayed packet has no destination reference because package
acknowledgement is handled by the persistence transition.

Prune records without an open circuit and propagate storage or decoding
errors. The store is not populated until the channel cleanup integration
lands in a later commit.

commit.message:
channeldb: add forwarding response store

Add a top-level store for forwarding settle and fail messages indexed by
outgoing circuit key. This aligns response lookup with the
circuit-oriented model already used for contract-court resolution
messages.

Keep each response in its original wire encoding so replay preserves
failure reasons, custom records and other message details.

This commit establishes the storage schema and access methods. Later
commits connect the store to switch startup and channel cleanup.

commit.message:
bolt12: re-encode offer spec vectors on write

The vector table decoded each vector and compared every record against the
expected hex, but never fed one back out. So the message-level Encode and the
bech32 writer were only ever tested against fixtures we wrote ourselves. Each
valid vector now has to reproduce its own string, which passes for all of them
today and fails if the writer gains an extra character.

Finding F45.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/11001#discussion_r3804868912

bolt12: assert sentinels in subtype decoders

Both decode tables matched error substrings where the decoder returns a
sentinel, so a reworded message would keep passing a test that no longer
proves anything. Four cases now use require.ErrorIs, and the rest stay on
substrings because they assert ad-hoc messages with no sentinel behind them.
The mixed idiom is the one TestDecodeChainsRecord already uses in this file.

Finding F10.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10941#discussion_r3599756449

bolt12: cover the amount overflow guard

The request side had a test for the offer_amount times quantity overflow, the
invoice side did not, and it was the only uncovered branch in the invoice
amount check. Verified by neutering the guard, which makes the new case accept
an invoice_amount of one against an authorized amount that wrapped to zero.

Finding F9.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10941#discussion_r3599755895

bolt12: round-trip an invoice with every field

The round trip populated six of thirty fields despite its name, and asserted
byte identity only, which cannot see a field wired into the encode path but
not into the decode path. Comparing the decoded struct against the fixture
catches it, verified by dropping invoice_relative_expiry from the decode
stream. The invoice is signed and read-validated too, so the fixture is one a
payer would accept.

Finding F31.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10832#discussion_r3422236322

bolt12: round-trip a full invoice request

The round trip covered four of twenty-one fields and asserted byte identity
only, which cannot see a field wired into the encode path but not into the
decode path. Comparing the decoded struct against the fixture catches it,
verified by dropping invreq_quantity from the decode stream. The request is
also signed rather than carrying a placeholder, so the fixture is one a reader
would accept.

Finding F31.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10832#discussion_r3422236322

bolt12: round-trip an offer with every field

The round trip covered four of eleven fields and asserted byte identity only.
Byte identity cannot see a field that is wired into the encode path but not
into the decode path: such a field survives as an unknown TLV and re-encodes
cleanly while its typed value disappears. Comparing the decoded struct against
the fixture catches it, verified by dropping offer_quantity_max from the decode
stream. The fixture also carries an unknown odd TLV in the offer range, so the
offer keeps the byte-exact preservation its siblings already pin.

Findings F31 and F2.
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10832#discussion_r3422236322
https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/10789#discussion_r3416301143
